evidence.observation: Plan: "U2–U6 and U8 skip every element whose origin is an include; those elements were validated standalone at resolution step 8 under their own file's rules". The section 6 control is "the attribution lines of VG3 name every include and its confirmed count on each validate". In src/gnd/model/_includes.py the standalone check keeps only `severity == 'error'` issues. D-03 (_validation.py:1409-1450, `semantic:modality-policy`) is only a warning for a proposed llm-inferred/common-sense/induced alethic constraint, and outside the unattended mode nothing refuses `explicit`/`user-supplied` without a reviewer. So a file the unattended host writes itself, with no mode, can carry proposed llm-inferred alethic constraints or explicit-sourced claims. Included, those bypass U3 and U8 under the root, and the attribution line counts only `confirmed`, so they are not even counted.

concerns.recommendation: Narrow the exemption: keep U8 (and the D-03 condition) for included constraints that are not `confirmed`, or require each included file to declare a non-`none` reviewer. Widen the D5 attribution to count alethic and unconfirmed-alethic constraints and non-proposed sources. Add a VG3 criterion where an included file with a proposed llm-inferred alethic constraint is refused, or at least flagged, under an unattended root. Section 6 should state the residual trust assumption as a named limit, not as a control.
concerns.title: Include exemption lets an unattended root carry unreviewed alethic or explicit claims as if reviewed

evidence.observation: R0.4 says root-owned elements are "checked by U1–U8 exactly as today", and section 6 claims "VG3-C2 and VG3-C3, one case per rule and one for an attached constraint". But VG3-C2 tests only "exit 3 with U2, U3, U4" and VG3-C3 only "U5". No case covers U6 (root-owned sample rows without sample_spans), U7 (a root-owned span naming an undeclared document) or U8 (a root-owned alethic sample/llm-inferred constraint). In _merge (_includes.py:162-167), a root constraint attached to an included fact type lands at `$.fact_types[k].constraints[n]` with origin 'model', inside a fact type whose origin is `includes[ID]`. An origin skip keyed on the fact type rather than the constraint would silently exempt it from U8.

concerns.recommendation: Extend VG3-C2/C3 to one root-owned case each for U6, U7 and U8, including a U8 case on an alethic `sample` constraint attached to an included fact type, so the shared origin test is pinned at constraint granularity.
concerns.title: R0.4 claims every U rule is kept, but the criteria test only U2–U5

evidence.location: VG3 goal; section 2 VG3; section 10 open questions
evidence.observation: The goal and section 2 exempt included elements from "U2–U6 and U8", which implies U7 still applies to them, yet the open questions defer "what U7 does with a span an included element carries". In _unattended.py:207-226, U7 is emitted only as span_rule_id inside the U4/U5/U6 walks, so skipping included elements in those walks also drops U7 for them. The plan's rule text and the code's structure point different ways. A reviewed seed's spans name documents the root does not declare, so applying U7 would refuse the #222 root that VG3-C1 requires to pass.

concerns.recommendation: Decide in the plan, not the spec, that U7 is exempt for included elements (consistent with VG3-C1 and VG3-C5), list it in the D3 exemption, and test it.
concerns.title: Whether U7 applies to included elements is unresolved and conflicts with VG3-C1

evidence.location: section 5 Compatibility; section 2 VG3 span walk; VG3-C5
evidence.observation: Plan: "VG2 (a) and VG3 (a) admit inputs that 0.4.0 refuses and refuse nothing 0.4.0 admits" and "0.4.0 admits no unattended include root at all (H14), so no shipped model is affected". Today _includes.py refuses only an included file whose own mode is unattended, and _rule_unattended runs over the merged document. So an unattended root whose included elements are proposed, not explicit, and carry spans citing a root-declared document validates in 0.4.0. H25's workaround, with the seed file as the root's first document, is that shape. For such roots, VG3-C5 ("span counts cover root-owned spans only") stops re-hashing the included spans that 0.4.0 checks, which changes `--require-documents` output and weakens integrity. D6 also refuses a repin-include that 0.4.0 admits on them.

concerns.recommendation: Correct the compatibility statement. Either keep re-hashing an included element's span when it names a document the root declares, or state the behaviour change, and add a criterion pinning a 0.4.0-valid unattended include root's validate output.
concerns.title: The claim that 0.4.0 admits no unattended include root is false, so VG3 changes output for valid roots

evidence.observation: VG3-C8: "an issue on an included object type carries `includes[ID]:` (H17)". H17's only producer is U4 on included object types, which VG3 exempts. The remaining `$.object_types[id=…]` diagnostics (_validation.py:628, 672, 697) are errors that a standalone-valid included file cannot raise. After VG3, no CLI path is left that produces the issue the criterion tests. If remap_issues is widened for every root, VG3-C7's "byte-identical `gnd validate` output" for non-unattended include roots also needs a check.

concerns.recommendation: Name the producer in the plan, or restate VG3-C8 as a unit test of remap_issues over a synthetic `$.object_types[id=…]` issue plus a VG3-C7 case on a non-unattended include root.
concerns.title: VG3-C8 has no reachable producer once the exemption lands

evidence.location: section 3 VG4 homes; section 9 VG4 lane
evidence.observation: VG4 changes "`src/gnd/model/_unattended.py` (U1)", but its homes and its lane (`tests/test_vg4_seeded_growth_rounds.py tests/test_mc3_evolution.py ... tests/test_unattended_model_growth_acceptance.py`) leave out tests/test_unattended_mode.py. That file holds the U1 table cases "u1-documents-absent" and "u1-documents-empty" (lines 120-121), which D4 (a) touches directly.

concerns.recommendation: Add tests/test_unattended_mode.py (and test_unattended_span_coverage.py) to VG4's homes and focused lane.
concerns.title: The VG4 lane skips the existing U1 tests that D4 changes

evidence.location: section 2 VG4 First document; VG4-C3; section 6 row 7
evidence.observation: Plan: "U1 admits a missing or empty `documents` list while the root owns no object type, fact type or constraint". _rule_unattended takes the composed document alone (H16), so on an include root "owns" has to come from origins. Root attachments live in `fact_type_constraints` and merge into included fact types. VG4-C3 tests only a root with "no owned element" and one "with an owned element" without saying which kind. Nothing pins a root that owns only an attached constraint, or that the relaxation leaves the `reviewer: none` half of U1 in force.

concerns.recommendation: Define 'owns' through the same origin test as VG3 (attachments count), and add VG4-C3 cases for a root owning only an attached constraint and for a document-less root with a non-`none` reviewer.
concerns.title: The D4 (a) U1 relaxation does not pin attachments or the reviewer half

evidence.observation: VG1-C1 asks that `denoting_types`, `descendant_closure` and `universe_types` "return what they return at the base commit", and the control is "against the base commit". Once VG1 replaces those walks, a test cannot run base-commit code unless a frozen expectation or a retained reference implementation exists. The plan names neither.

concerns.recommendation: State that VG1 commits a golden snapshot generated at 4ad0d216 (or keeps the old walks as a test-only reference) and compares against it.
concerns.title: VG1-C1's base-commit comparison needs a stated oracle

evidence.observation: VG1-C2/C3 require "under 10 s in process" and VG1-C5 "under 20 s", calibrated from measurements made "on one laptop, once". These absolute bounds depend on the machine. The headroom is large (H29: 0.48–1.29 s), but the criterion is still a wall-clock threshold rather than a property of the code.

concerns.recommendation: Make the doubling ratio the primary criterion. Express the absolute bound relative to a same-run baseline (for example, at most k times the 0-extra-types run), or put it in the slow lane, as section 9 already allows for the ratio.
concerns.title: VG1's absolute time bounds depend on the machine

evidence.location: D9; section 3 VG1 homes; section 4 VG1
evidence.observation: D9 proposes that "VG1 measures `gnd verify` at 1,000 extra types" and may give the oracle walk its own table. No VG1 criterion records that measurement, and VG1's homes do not list `src/gnd/synth/oracle/constructive.py`. Separately, R0.4 reads "An element the root owns, a constraint the root attaches to an included fact type included, is checked", a garbled sentence.

concerns.recommendation: Add a VG1 criterion for the gnd verify measurement and its conditional home, and fix the wording of R0.4.
concerns.title: D9's measurement has no criterion or home, and R0.4 is garbled

summary: The plan's code and document citations match the checkout (universe.py:59/218/299/358, semantic_adapter.py:610-611/707, _includes.py:222-237 and remap_issues, _enforce_d12 at service.py:402-477, evolution contract lines 258/279-280/618-664, representation-format.md:1845-1847/1905-1915, pyproject.toml:79). The phase order is acyclic, and VG4 is mostly a pin of today's evolve include behaviour: enforce_ownership already makes included elements read-only, and ConstraintLocator host included_fact_type already exists. D2 (a) admits nothing that U5 or U8 should refuse. Nothing blocks the demonstration. The main gaps: the D3 (a) exemption lets an unattended host include a self-authored, unreviewed file and bypass U2/U3/U8, and the attribution control does not close that. The R0.4 criteria test only U2-U5, not U6-U8. U7's status is ambiguous. The compatibility claim that 0.4.0 admits no unattended include root is false, so VG3-C5 changes the output of roots 0.4.0 admits. VG3-C8 has nothing left to produce it. The VG4 lane omits the existing U1 tests.
